scope: Deuteronomy 13–18, all 134 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Deuteronomy 13:1–18 binds Hebrew 13:2–19; chapters 14–18 align directly. Hebrew 13:1 is excluded because the preceding batch binds it to public 12:32. All 134 original XML records, including their written/read and numbering notes, are hashed in full.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Opens the conditional sentence across verse labels; preserves prophet and dreamer as two descriptions and both sign terms.
verses.before: “If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises in your midst and gives you a sign or wonder,
verses.after: “If a prophet or someone who dreams dreams appears among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises in your midst and gives you a sign or wonder,

verses.rationale: Keeps the sign's actual fulfillment; the problem is the invitation to other gods, not a failed prediction.
verses.before: and the sign or wonder that he spoke to you happens, saying, ‘Let us go after other gods whom you have not known and let us serve them,’
verses.after: and the sign or wonder comes true, but that person says, ‘Let us follow other gods’—gods you have not known—‘and serve them,’
verses.tsw_comparator: and the sign or wonder that he spoke to you comes to pass, saying, ‘Let us go after other gods whom you have not known and let us serve them,’

verses.rationale: Retains God's testing to know and the full heart-and-soul formula without explaining away the stated purpose.
verses.before: you will not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for the LORD your God is testing you to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your life.
verses.after: do not listen to that prophet or dreamer. The LORD your God is testing you to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for the LORD your God is testing you to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your life.

verses.rationale: Keeps all six allegiance verbs, using two sentences to make the sequence audible.
verses.before: After the LORD your God you will walk, him you will fear, his commandments you will keep, his voice you will listen to, him you will serve, and to him you will cling.
verses.after: Follow the LORD your God and fear him. Keep his commands, listen to his voice, serve him, and hold fast to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the LORD your God you shall walk, him you shall fear, his commandments you shall keep, his voice you shall listen to, him you shall serve, and to him you shall cling.

verses.rationale: States execution and its grounds explicitly; preserves redemption, walking imagery, and the recurring purge formula.
verses.before: But that prophet or that dreamer of dreams will be put to death, because he spoke rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to turn you aside from the way in which the LORD your God commanded you to walk. So you will remove the evil from your midst.
verses.after: That prophet or dreamer must be put to death for urging rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. That person tried to turn you from the way the LORD your God commanded you to walk. You must purge the evil from among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But that prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because he spoke rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to turn you aside from the way in which the LORD your God commanded you to walk. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.

verses.rationale: Retains the specifically maternal brother, wife of the bosom, and friend like one's own life rather than flattening the list to relatives.
verses.before: “If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son, your daughter, the wife of your embrace, or your companion who is as your own life secretly entices you, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods,’ whom you and your ancestors have not known,
verses.after: Suppose your brother, your own mother's son, or your son or daughter, or the wife you embrace, or a friend as dear as your own life secretly entices you, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods’—gods neither you nor your ancestors have known,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son, your daughter, the wife of your embrace, or your companion who is as your own life secretly entices you, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods,’ whom you and your ancestors have not known,

verses.rationale: Completes the enticement's object across labels and preserves both distance contrasts.
verses.before: from the gods of the peoples who are around you, near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other,
verses.after: gods of the peoples around you, near or far, from one end of the earth to the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: from the gods of the peoples who are around you, near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other,

verses.rationale: Preserves refusal, the eye-of-pity image, and the distinct prohibitions against sparing and concealing.
verses.before: you will not consent to him or listen to him. Your eye will not pity him; you will not spare him or conceal him.
verses.after: Do not agree or listen. Do not let your eye pity that person; do not spare or shield them.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall not consent to him or listen to him. Your eye shall not pity him; you shall not spare him or conceal him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the addressee's first participation in killing, followed by the community; does not soften the law to exclusion.
verses.before: Rather, you will surely put him to death. Your hand will be first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.
verses.after: You must put that person to death. Your hand must be the first raised to kill them, followed by the hands of all the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rather, you shall surely put him to death. Your hand shall be first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.

verses.rationale: Names the lethal method and repeats the slavery-deliverance ground rather than replacing it with a cross-reference.
verses.before: You will stone him with stones so that he dies, because he sought to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.
verses.after: Stone that person to death for trying to turn you from the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall stone him with stones so that he dies, because he sought to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.

verses.rationale: Renders hearing and fear as the stated deterrent purpose, without recasting fear as mere respect.
verses.before: Then all Israel will hear and fear and will not again do such an evil thing in your midst.
verses.after: Then all Israel will hear and be afraid, and no one among you will do such an evil thing again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all Israel will hear and fear and will not again do such an evil thing in your midst.

verses.rationale: Begins the reported-town case and leaves its content connected to the following label.
verses.before: “If you hear in one of your cities that the LORD your God is giving you to live in,
verses.after: Suppose you hear a report about one of the towns the LORD your God is giving you to live in,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If you hear in one of your cities that the LORD your God is giving you to live in,

verses.rationale: Renders sons of belial as wicked men, not a reference to a named supernatural being; preserves their origin within Israel.
verses.before: ‘Worthless men have gone out from your midst and led the inhabitants of their city astray, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods whom you have not known,”’
verses.after: that wicked men have gone out from among you and led the town's inhabitants astray, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods’—gods you have not known.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Worthless men have gone out from your midst and led the inhabitants of their city astray, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods whom you have not known,”’

verses.rationale: Keeps the three investigative verbs and the requirement of an established report before the penalty.
verses.before: then you will inquire, search, and investigate carefully. And look, if the thing is true and established that this detestable thing has been done in your midst,
verses.after: You must inquire, investigate, and question thoroughly. If the report is true and it is established that this detestable thing has been done among you,
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall inquire, search, and investigate carefully. And look, if the thing is true and established that this detestable thing has been done in your midst,

verses.rationale: Retains collective killing, livestock, and repeated sword language; that town follows the feminine reading without duplicating the written/read pronoun.
verses.before: you will surely strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword. Devote it and all that is in it to destruction, including its livestock, with the edge of the sword.
verses.after: you must strike down that town's inhabitants with the sword. Devote the town and everything in it to destruction, including its livestock, by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall surely strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword. Devote it and all that is in it to destruction, including its livestock, with the edge of the sword.

verses.rationale: Keeps the central square, complete burning to God, perpetual ruin, and rebuilding prohibition; whole offering renders kalil without substituting the usual burnt-offering noun.
verses.before: You will gather all its spoil into the middle of its open square and burn the city and all its spoil with fire as a whole offering to the LORD your God. It will be a ruin forever; it will not be rebuilt.
verses.after: Gather all its plunder into the middle of its square. Burn the town and all its plunder as a whole offering to the LORD your God. It must remain a mound of ruins forever, never to be rebuilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall gather all its spoil into the middle of its open square and burn the city and all its spoil with fire as a whole offering to the LORD your God. It shall be a ruin forever; it shall not be rebuilt.

verses.rationale: Preserves the clinging-to-hand image, distinct mercy terms, and population increase under the ancestral oath.
verses.before: Nothing from what is devoted to destruction will cling to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from his burning anger and give you compassion and have compassion on you and multiply you, as he swore to your ancestors,
verses.after: Let nothing devoted to destruction cling to your hand. Then the LORD will turn from his fierce anger, show you mercy and compassion, and increase your numbers as he swore to your ancestors,
verses.tsw_comparator: Nothing from what is devoted to destruction shall cling to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from his burning anger and give you compassion and have compassion on you and multiply you, as he swore to your ancestors,

verses.rationale: Completes the obedience condition and retains the divine-eye standard at the close of Moses' chapter speech.
verses.before: when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all his commandments that I command you today and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
verses.after: as you listen to the LORD your God, keeping all his commands that I give you today and doing what is right in his eyes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all his commandments that I command you today and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Renders collective sons inclusively while retaining the bodily location and the specific mourning setting of both prohibitions.
verses.before: “You are children of the LORD your God. You will not cut yourselves or make baldness between your eyes for the dead.
verses.after: “You are children of the LORD your God. Do not cut yourselves or shave a bald patch above your eyes in mourning for the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You are children of the LORD your God. You shall not cut yourselves or make baldness between your eyes for the dead.

verses.rationale: Keeps holy identity, divine choice, and treasure language as the grounds for the instructions.
verses.before: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be for him a treasured people from all the peoples who are on the face of the ground.
verses.after: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the ground, the LORD chose you to be his treasured people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be for him a treasured people from all the peoples who are on the face of the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains the compact opening prohibition without importing the later animal categories into it.
verses.before: “You will not eat any detestable thing.
verses.after: Do not eat anything detestable.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not eat any detestable thing.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three domestic kinds and joins their list to the seven wild kinds in the next label.
verses.before: These are the animals that you may eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat;
verses.after: These are the animals you may eat: cattle, sheep, goats,
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the animals that you may eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat;

verses.rationale: Represents all seven Hebrew wild-animal names individually; approximate species identifications are qualified in a note.
verses.before: the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
verses.after: deer, gazelle, fallow deer, wild goat, antelope, wild ox, and mountain sheep.
verses.tsw_comparator: the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.

verses.rationale: Makes the conjunction of both physical criteria explicit without presenting either criterion as sufficient alone.
verses.before: Every animal that divides the hoof, having the hoof split in two, and chews the cud among the animals, you may eat.
verses.after: You may eat any animal that has a hoof divided into two parts and also chews the cud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every animal that divides the hoof, having the hoof split in two, and chews the cud among the animals, you may eat.

verses.rationale: Preserves the source's classification of hare and hyrax rather than rewriting the ancient description to modern zoology.
verses.before: But these you will not eat from those that chew the cud or divide the split hoof: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger, for they chew the cud but do not divide the hoof; they are unclean for you.
verses.after: But among animals that chew the cud or have divided hooves, do not eat the camel, the hare, or the hyrax. They chew the cud but do not have divided hooves, so they are unclean for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But these you shall not eat from those that chew the cud or divide the split hoof: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger, for they chew the cud but do not divide the hoof; they are unclean for you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pig's contrasting criteria and the plural carcasses that extends back over the prohibited animals.
verses.before: And the pig, because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. You will not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses.
verses.after: The pig is also unclean for you: it has divided hooves but does not chew the cud. Do not eat their meat or touch their carcasses.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the pig, because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses.

verses.rationale: Retains both required water-creature features in a short positive rule.
verses.before: “These you may eat from all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales you may eat.
verses.after: Of all the creatures in the water, you may eat those with fins and scales.
verses.tsw_comparator: “These you may eat from all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales you may eat.

verses.rationale: Preserves the matching negative rule and its ritual classification.
verses.before: But whatever does not have fins and scales you will not eat; it is unclean for you.
verses.after: Do not eat any that do not have both fins and scales; they are unclean for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But whatever does not have fins and scales you shall not eat; it is unclean for you.

verses.rationale: Leaves the concise permission intact as the opening to the flying-creature list.
verses.before: “Every clean bird you may eat.
verses.after: You may eat any clean bird.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Every clean bird you may eat.

verses.rationale: Uses the established Fluent equivalents for nesher, peres, and ozniyah; species uncertainty is explicit in the apparatus.
verses.before: But these are the ones you will not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the black vulture;
verses.after: But these you must not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
verses.tsw_comparator: But these are the ones you shall not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the black vulture;

verses.rationale: Preserves all three Hebrew names raah, ayyah, and dayyah; transliterates the uncertain third term rather than silently dropping it or harmonizing Leviticus.
verses.before: the red kite, the falcon, and the kite according to its kind;
verses.after: the kite, the falcon, every kind of dayyah,
verses.tsw_comparator: the red kite, the falcon, and the kite according to its kind;

verses.rationale: Keeps the separate raven category and its every-kind qualifier within the continuous list.
verses.before: every raven according to its kind;
verses.after: every kind of raven,
verses.tsw_comparator: every raven according to its kind;

verses.rationale: Represents the four source names in order with provisional English identifications consistent with the earlier list.
verses.before: the ostrich, the owl, the gull, and the hawk according to its kind;
verses.after: the ostrich, the nighthawk, the gull, every kind of hawk,
verses.tsw_comparator: the ostrich, the owl, the gull, and the hawk according to its kind;

verses.rationale: Keeps kos, yanshuf, and tinshemet in Deuteronomy's order rather than copying Leviticus' different sequence.
verses.before: the little owl, the great owl, and the white owl;
verses.after: the little owl, the great owl, the barn owl,
verses.tsw_comparator: the little owl, the great owl, and the white owl;

verses.rationale: Preserves qaat, rachamah, and shalakh as three distinct entries with qualified species equivalents.
verses.before: the pelican, the carrion vulture, and the cormorant;
verses.after: the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
verses.tsw_comparator: the pelican, the carrion vulture, and the cormorant;

verses.rationale: Retains the bat in the source's flying-creature category and limits every kind to the heron entry.
verses.before: the stork and the heron according to its kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
verses.after: the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
verses.tsw_comparator: the stork and the heron according to its kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.

verses.rationale: Keeps the broader swarming category and repeated prohibition rather than substituting a modern taxonomic list.
verses.before: Every winged swarming thing is unclean for you; they will not be eaten.
verses.after: All winged swarming creatures are unclean for you. They must not be eaten.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every winged swarming thing is unclean for you; they shall not be eaten.

verses.rationale: Preserves the closing permission and the broader flying-creature term oph.
verses.before: Every clean flying creature you may eat.
verses.after: You may eat any clean flying creature.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every clean flying creature you may eat.

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinction between resident foreigner and foreigner, the two disposal permissions, and the specific goat-and-milk prohibition.
verses.before: “You will not eat anything that dies by itself. You may give it to the resident alien who is within your gates so that he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner, for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. You will not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
verses.after: Do not eat an animal found dead. You may give it to the resident foreigner in your town to eat, or sell it to a foreigner. For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not eat anything that dies by itself. You may give it to the resident alien who is within your gates so that he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner, for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.

verses.rationale: Retains annual frequency, all produce, and the agricultural basis of the tithe.
verses.before: “You will surely tithe all the produce of your seed that comes out from the field year by year.
verses.after: Set aside a tenth of all the produce from the seed you sow, all that your field yields year after year.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed that comes out from the field year by year.

verses.rationale: Keeps the specified foods, firstborn, chosen-name place, and learning-to-fear purpose rather than generalizing the meal as celebration alone.
verses.before: You will eat before the LORD your God, in the place that he will choose to make his name dwell there, the tithe of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herd and flock, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God all the days.
verses.after: Eat the tithe of your grain, new wine, and oil, along with the firstborn of your herds and flocks, before the LORD your God at the place he chooses for his name to dwell. In this way you will learn to fear the LORD your God always.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall eat before the LORD your God, in the place that he will choose to make his name dwell there, the tithe of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herd and flock, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God all the days.

verses.rationale: Keeps distance, inability to carry, and blessing together in the conditional sentence.
verses.before: But if the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it because the place that the LORD your God will choose to put his name there is too far from you, when the LORD your God blesses you,
verses.after: But if the journey is too long for you to carry it, because the place the LORD your God chooses for his name is far away and the LORD your God has blessed you,
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it because the place that the LORD your God will choose to put his name there is too far from you, when the LORD your God blesses you,

verses.rationale: Preserves silver and the concrete hand-carrying image instead of substituting an abstract payment system.
verses.before: then you will turn it into silver, bind the silver in your hand, and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
verses.after: turn it into silver, tie up the silver in your hand, and travel to the place the LORD your God chooses.
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall turn it into silver, bind the silver in your hand, and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose.

verses.rationale: Retains permission for wine and shekhar alongside livestock and household joy; a note prevents strong drink from implying modern distilled spirits.
verses.before: You may spend the silver for whatever your life desires: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or whatever your life asks of you. You will eat there before the LORD your God, and you will rejoice, you and your household.
verses.after: Spend the silver on whatever you desire—cattle, sheep and goats, wine, strong drink, or anything else you wish. Eat there before the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may spend the silver for whatever your life desires: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or whatever your life asks of you. You shall eat there before the LORD your God, and you shall rejoice, you and your household.

verses.rationale: Keeps the local Levite's lack of allotted inheritance as the explicit ground of provision.
verses.before: And the Levite who is within your gates you will not abandon, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.
verses.after: Do not neglect the Levite in your town, who has no share or inheritance with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Levite who is within your gates you shall not abandon, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the third-year local deposit from the annual journey meal, retaining that year's whole tithe.
verses.before: “At the end of every three years you will bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year and deposit it within your gates.
verses.after: At the end of every three years, bring out the whole tithe of that year's produce and store it in your towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At the end of every three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year and deposit it within your gates.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four recipient groups, the repeated Levitical rationale, satisfaction, and the work-of-hands blessing.
verses.before: Then the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who are within your gates will come and eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.
verses.after: Then the Levite, who has no share or inheritance with you, and the resident foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow in your towns can come and eat their fill. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who are within your gates shall come and eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.

verses.rationale: Supplies debts from the following rule while retaining release as the key term; apparatus acknowledges disagreement about permanent remission versus suspension.
verses.before: “At the end of every seven years you will make a release.
verses.after: “At the end of every seven years, grant a release of debts.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At the end of every seven years you shall make a release.

verses.rationale: Retains creditor action, the neighbor/brother relationship, and the proclamation without silently deciding the disputed duration of release.
verses.before: And this is the manner of the release: every creditor will release what he has lent to his neighbor. He will not press his neighbor or his brother, because the LORD’s release has been proclaimed.
verses.after: This is how the release works: every creditor must release the claim on what they have lent their neighbor. They must not press their neighbor, their fellow Israelite, for payment, because the LORD's release has been proclaimed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor. He shall not press his neighbor or his brother, because the LORD’s release has been proclaimed.

verses.rationale: Preserves the law's unequal treatment of foreigner and fellow Israelite instead of universalizing the permission.
verses.before: You may press a foreigner, but whatever of yours is with your brother your hand will release.
verses.after: You may demand payment from a foreigner, but you must release your claim on whatever your fellow Israelite owes you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may press a foreigner, but whatever of yours is with your brother your hand shall release.

verses.rationale: Keeps the no-poor assurance tied grammatically to the next verse's condition, without harmonizing away verse 11.
verses.before: “Indeed, there should be no poor among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess,
verses.after: Yet there should be no poor among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess as an inheritance,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Indeed, there should be no poor among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess,

verses.rationale: Retains the restrictive obedience condition rather than presenting verse 4 as an unconditional prediction.
verses.before: if only you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all this commandment that I command you today.
verses.after: if only you listen carefully to the LORD your God and take care to carry out every command I give you today.
verses.tsw_comparator: if only you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all this commandment that I command you today.

verses.rationale: Preserves both lending/borrowing and ruling/being-ruled contrasts with repeated many nations.
verses.before: For the LORD your God will bless you as he spoke to you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
verses.after: The LORD your God will bless you as he promised. You will lend to many nations but borrow from none. You will rule over many nations, and they will not rule over you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God will bless you as he spoke to you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the land-and-town scope and paired heart/hand images, with brother understood as fellow Israelite.
verses.before: “If there is among you a poor person, one of your brothers, within one of your gates in your land that the LORD your God is giving you, you will not harden your heart or close your hand against your poor brother.
verses.after: If anyone among your fellow Israelites is poor in any town in the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not harden your heart or close your hand against your poor neighbor.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If there is among you a poor person, one of your brothers, within one of your gates in your land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall not harden your heart or close your hand against your poor brother.

verses.rationale: Retains lending, not only charitable giving, and the emphatic open-hand instruction with need as the measure.
verses.before: Rather, you will surely open your hand to him and surely lend him enough for his need, whatever he lacks.
verses.after: Open your hand wide. Lend enough to meet the need.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rather, you shall surely open your hand to him and surely lend him enough for his need, whatever he lacks.

verses.rationale: Makes the release-year calculation audible as inner speech; retains grudging sight, withholding, the poor person's appeal, and liability for sin.
verses.before: Guard yourself, lest there be a worthless thought in your heart, saying, ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is near,’ and your eye be evil against your poor brother and you give him nothing. Then he may cry against you to the LORD, and it will be sin in you.
verses.after: Watch out for this wicked thought in your heart: ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is near.’ Do not look grudgingly at your poor neighbor and give nothing. Your neighbor may cry to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Guard yourself, lest there be a worthless thought in your heart, saying, ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is near,’ and your eye be evil against your poor brother and you give him nothing. Then he may cry against you to the LORD, and it will be sin in you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic giving verb and heart disposition without importing an added loan formula from other witnesses.
verses.before: You will surely give to him, and your heart will not be grieved when you give to him, for because of this thing the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in all to which you put your hand.
verses.after: Give generously, without a grudging heart. Because of this, the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and everything you undertake.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall surely give to him, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give to him, for because of this thing the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in all to which you put your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit ongoing poverty statement alongside verse 4's conditional assurance, and repeats the open-hand image.
verses.before: For the poor will never cease from the midst of the land. Therefore I command you, saying, ‘You will surely open your hand to your brother, to your needy and to your poor in your land.’
verses.after: There will always be poor people in the land. That is why I command you to open your hand wide to your fellow Israelite, to the poor and needy in your land.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the poor will never cease from the midst of the land. Therefore I command you, saying, ‘You shall surely open your hand to your brother, to your needy and to your poor in your land.’

verses.rationale: Names sale, both sexes, six years of service and seventh-year freedom; does not present slavery as ordinary employment.
verses.before: “If your brother, a Hebrew man or Hebrew woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you will send that person free from you.
verses.after: If one of your people, a Hebrew man or woman, is sold to you and serves you for six years, you must set that person free in the seventh year.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If your brother, a Hebrew man or Hebrew woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you shall send that person free from you.

verses.rationale: Uses the inclusive pronoun for the man or woman in verse 12 while retaining the concrete empty-hands prohibition.
verses.before: And when you send that person free from you, you will not send him away empty-handed.
verses.after: When you set them free, do not send them away empty-handed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you send that person free from you, you shall not send him away empty-handed.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three agricultural sources and makes God's blessing the basis of generous departure provisions.
verses.before: You will surely furnish him from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. From that with which the LORD your God has blessed you, you will give to him.
verses.after: Supply them generously from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Give to them from the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall surely furnish him from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. From that with which the LORD your God has blessed you, you shall give to him.

verses.rationale: Retains slavery and redemption as the stated memory grounding this law, not merely a general appeal to kindness.
verses.before: You will remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you. Therefore I command you this thing today.
verses.after: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I give you this command today.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you. Therefore I command you this thing today.

verses.rationale: Returns to the source's male example and preserves the stated motives without implying every slave's situation was chosen.
verses.before: But if he says to you, ‘I will not go out from you,’ because he loves you and your household, because it is good for him with you,
verses.after: But suppose he says to you, ‘I will not leave you,’ because he loves you and your household and is well off with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if he says to you, ‘I will not go out from you,’ because he loves you and your household, because it is good for him with you,

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily piercing, the door, permanent slavery, and the female-slave clause; the note flags the disputed scope of do the same.
verses.before: then you will take an awl and put it through his ear into the door, and he will be your servant permanently. You will do likewise to your female servant.
verses.after: Then take an awl and drive it through his ear into the door. He will be your slave permanently. Do the same for your female slave.
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall take an awl and put it through his ear into the door, and he shall be your servant permanently. You shall do likewise to your female servant.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult double-wage comparison rather than changing six years to a presumed hired-worker contract length.
verses.before: It will not be difficult in your eyes when you send him free from you, for six years he has served you for twice the wages of a hired worker. And the LORD your God will bless you in all that you do.
verses.after: Do not resent setting your slave free. Those six years of service have been worth twice the wages of a hired worker. The LORD your God will bless you in everything you do.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall not be difficult in your eyes when you send him free from you, for six years he has served you for twice the wages of a hired worker. And the LORD your God will bless you in all that you do.

verses.rationale: Keeps male firstborn, consecration, and the separate work and wool prohibitions.
verses.before: “Every firstborn male born in your herd or flock you will consecrate to the LORD your God. You will not work with the firstborn of your ox or shear the firstborn of your flock.
verses.after: Consecrate to the LORD your God every firstborn male from your herds and flocks. Do not put a firstborn ox to work or shear a firstborn animal from your flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Every firstborn male born in your herd or flock you shall consecrate to the LORD your God. You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox or shear the firstborn of your flock.

verses.rationale: Preserves the recurring household meal, divine presence, and chosen location.
verses.before: Before the LORD your God you and your household will eat it year by year in the place that the LORD will choose.
verses.after: Year after year, you and your household are to eat them before the LORD your God at the place the LORD chooses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before the LORD your God you and your household shall eat it year by year in the place that the LORD will choose.

verses.rationale: Retains both named defects and the broader blemish category as the condition excluding sacrifice.
verses.before: But if there is a defect in it—lameness, blindness, or any serious defect—you will not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
verses.after: But if an animal has a defect—lameness, blindness, or any serious blemish—do not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if there is a defect in it—lameness, blindness, or any serious defect—you shall not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps ordinary local eating open to both ritual-status groups and repeats the wild-game comparison.
verses.before: Within your gates you may eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as the gazelle and the deer.
verses.after: You may eat it in your towns, the unclean and the clean together, just as you eat gazelle or deer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Within your gates you may eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as the gazelle and the deer.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic blood exception and the water comparison, with a full chapter close.
verses.before: Only you will not eat its blood; you will pour it out upon the ground like water.
verses.after: Only do not eat its blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Only you shall not eat its blood; you shall pour it out upon the ground like water.

verses.rationale: Retains the named month twice, Passover, the exodus ground, and its nighttime setting.
verses.before: “Keep the month of Abib and make the Passover to the LORD your God, for in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out from Egypt by night.
verses.after: “Observe the month of Abib and keep the Passover to the LORD your God, because in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Keep the month of Abib and make the Passover to the LORD your God, for in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out from Egypt by night.

verses.rationale: Preserves both flock and herd rather than narrowing this festival instruction to the animal specification in Exodus 12.
verses.before: You will sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God from flock and herd in the place that the LORD will choose to make his name dwell there.
verses.after: Sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God from your flocks and herds, at the place the LORD chooses for his name to dwell.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God from flock and herd in the place that the LORD will choose to make his name dwell there.

verses.rationale: Keeps seven days, bread of affliction, haste, and lifelong remembrance as distinct details; retains full original record with its accent note.
verses.before: You will not eat leavened bread with it. Seven days you will eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, for in haste you came out from the land of Egypt, so that you may remember the day of your coming out from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
verses.after: Do not eat leavened bread with it. For seven days eat unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, because you left Egypt in haste. Do this so that you remember the day you came out of Egypt all the days of your life.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not eat leavened bread with it. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, for in haste you came out from the land of Egypt, so that you may remember the day of your coming out from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the seven-day territorial leaven ban from the first evening's overnight meat limit.
verses.before: No leaven will be seen with you in all your territory for seven days, and none of the flesh that you sacrifice in the evening on the first day will remain overnight until morning.
verses.after: No leaven is to be seen anywhere in your territory for seven days. None of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day may remain until morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: No leaven shall be seen with you in all your territory for seven days, and none of the flesh that you sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall remain overnight until morning.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prohibition on selecting an ordinary local town, preparing for the chosen-place exception.
verses.before: You may not sacrifice the Passover within any of your gates that the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.after: You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any town the LORD your God gives you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may not sacrifice the Passover within any of your gates that the LORD your God is giving you.

verses.rationale: Preserves exclusive location and all three temporal expressions without adding a modern clock time.
verses.before: Rather, at the place that the LORD your God will choose to make his name dwell there, you will sacrifice the Passover in the evening at sunset, at the appointed time of your coming out from Egypt.
verses.after: Sacrifice it only at the place the LORD your God chooses for his name to dwell, in the evening at sunset, at the time you came out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rather, at the place that the LORD your God will choose to make his name dwell there, you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening at sunset, at the appointed time of your coming out from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Renders bashal as cook, acknowledging its boiling sense in a note rather than forcing Exodus' roasting language into this clause.
verses.before: You will cook it and eat it at the place that the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you will turn and go to your tents.
verses.after: Cook it and eat it at the place the LORD your God chooses. In the morning you may turn back and go to your tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall cook it and eat it at the place that the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents.

verses.rationale: Keeps the six-plus-seventh formulation alongside the earlier seven-day instruction, with the seventh day's assembly and work ban.
verses.before: Six days you will eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there will be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God. You will do no work.
verses.after: For six days eat unleavened bread. On the seventh day hold a solemn assembly to the LORD your God; do no work.
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God. You shall do no work.

verses.rationale: Retains the agricultural starting point, sickle imagery, and seven-week count without inserting a fixed date.
verses.before: “You will count seven weeks for yourself. From the time the sickle first begins to cut the standing grain, you will begin to count seven weeks.
verses.after: Count seven weeks. Begin counting when the sickle first cuts the standing grain.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall count seven weeks for yourself. From the time the sickle first begins to cut the standing grain, you shall begin to count seven weeks.

verses.rationale: Preserves the festival name, voluntary offering, hand image, and measure according to blessing.
verses.before: Then you will make the Festival of Weeks to the LORD your God with the measure of a freewill offering from your hand, which you will give according to how the LORD your God blesses you.
verses.after: Then keep the Festival of Weeks to the LORD your God with a freewill offering from your hand, in proportion to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall make the Festival of Weeks to the LORD your God with the measure of a freewill offering from your hand, which you shall give according to how the LORD your God blesses you.

verses.rationale: Keeps every named participant, including explicitly enslaved men and women, within the chosen-place celebration.
verses.before: You will rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite who is within your gates, and the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who are in your midst—at the place that the LORD your God will choose to make his name dwell there.
verses.after: Rejoice before the LORD your God at the place he chooses for his name to dwell—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slave, the Levite in your towns, and the resident foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite who is within your gates, and the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who are in your midst—at the place that the LORD your God will choose to make his name dwell there.

verses.rationale: Retains slavery memory and the imperative to practice these statutes at the close of the Weeks instruction.
verses.before: You will remember that you were a servant in Egypt, and you will keep and do these statutes.
verses.after: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and take care to carry out these statutes.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall remember that you were a servant in Egypt, and you shall keep and do these statutes.

verses.rationale: Preserves Booths, its seven-day duration, and both harvest locations.
verses.before: “You will make the Festival of Booths for yourself seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and your winepress.
verses.after: Keep the Festival of Booths for seven days, when you gather in the produce from your threshing floor and winepress.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall make the Festival of Booths for yourself seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and your winepress.

verses.rationale: Repeats all participant categories instead of replacing the second list with everyone, allowing readers to hear the law's emphasis.
verses.before: You will rejoice in your festival—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite, the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who are within your gates.
verses.after: Rejoice at your festival—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slave, the Levite, the resident foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow in your towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall rejoice in your festival—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite, the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who are within your gates.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated seven days, chosen place, twofold blessing, and emphatic joy conclusion without promising an absence of all sorrow.
verses.before: Seven days you will celebrate to the LORD your God at the place that the LORD will choose, for the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you will be altogether joyful.
verses.after: For seven days celebrate to the LORD your God at the place the LORD chooses. The LORD your God will bless all your produce and all the work of your hands, and you are to be wholly joyful.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven days you shall celebrate to the LORD your God at the place that the LORD will choose, for the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be altogether joyful.

verses.rationale: Preserves the specifically male appearance requirement alongside the earlier inclusive feast lists, all three names, and the gift requirement.
verses.before: “Three times in the year every male among you will appear before the LORD your God at the place that he will choose: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, at the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Booths. No one will appear before the LORD empty-handed.
verses.after: Three times a year all your males must appear before the LORD your God at the place he chooses: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths. No one is to appear before the LORD empty-handed.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Three times in the year every male among you shall appear before the LORD your God at the place that he will choose: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, at the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Booths. No one shall appear before the LORD empty-handed.

verses.rationale: Keeps individual proportional giving rather than inventing a fixed amount.
verses.before: Each will give according to the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that he has given you.
verses.after: Each is to bring a gift in keeping with the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each shall give according to the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that he has given you.

verses.rationale: Retains both officials, tribal organization, every-town scope, and righteous judgment as their task.
verses.before: “You will appoint judges and officers for yourself within all your gates that the LORD your God is giving you according to your tribes, and they will judge the people with righteous judgment.
verses.after: Appoint judges and officers for your tribes in every town the LORD your God gives you. They must judge the people with justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall appoint judges and officers for yourself within all your gates that the LORD your God is giving you according to your tribes, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three prohibitions and both bribery images, including words rather than only a generalized corrupt outcome.
verses.before: You will not distort justice. You will not show partiality, and you will not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
verses.after: Do not twist justice, show favoritism, or accept a bribe. A bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not distort justice. You shall not show partiality, and you shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic repetition and connects the pursuit of justice with life and possession of the land.
verses.before: Justice, justice you will pursue, so that you may live and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.after: Justice, justice you must pursue, so that you may live and possess the land the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Justice, justice you shall pursue, so that you may live and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the planting/tree wording and the altar's proximity rather than reducing the command to a generic idol ban.
verses.before: “You will not plant for yourself an Asherah of any kind of tree beside the altar of the LORD your God that you make for yourself.
verses.after: Do not plant any tree as an Asherah beside the altar you make for the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not plant for yourself an Asherah of any kind of tree beside the altar of the LORD your God that you make for yourself.

verses.rationale: Keeps the separate stone prohibition and the explicit divine hatred rather than a milder statement of preference.
verses.before: And you will not set up for yourself a pillar, which the LORD your God hates.
verses.after: Do not set up a standing stone; the LORD your God hates it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall not set up for yourself a pillar, which the LORD your God hates.

verses.rationale: Retains both animal classes and the broad defect prohibition as a continuation of proper worship.
verses.before: “You will not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or sheep that has a defect, any serious flaw, for that is a detestable thing to the LORD your God.
verses.after: “Do not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or an animal from your flock with a blemish or any defect. That is detestable to the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or sheep that has a defect, any serious flaw, for that is a detestable thing to the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps both sexes, local discovery, the divine-eye standard, and covenant breach in the conditional opening.
verses.before: “If there is found in your midst, within one of your gates that the LORD your God is giving you, a man or woman who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God by transgressing his covenant,
verses.after: Suppose a man or woman is found among you, in one of the towns the LORD your God gives you, doing evil in the eyes of the LORD your God by breaking his covenant,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If there is found in your midst, within one of your gates that the LORD your God is giving you, a man or woman who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God by transgressing his covenant,

verses.rationale: Preserves the named celestial objects and the unexpected first-person command formula rather than silently replacing I with God.
verses.before: and goes and serves other gods and bows down to them, or to the sun, moon, or any of the host of the heavens, which I have not commanded,
verses.after: going to serve other gods and bowing down to them—to the sun, the moon, or any of the host of heaven—which I have not commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: and goes and serves other gods and bows down to them, or to the sun, moon, or any of the host of the heavens, which I have not commanded,

verses.rationale: Retains report, hearing, investigation, and established truth as prerequisites, continuing the case into the penalty.
verses.before: and it is told to you and you hear of it, then you will inquire carefully. And look, if the thing is true and established that this detestable thing has been done in Israel,
verses.after: When this is reported and you hear of it, investigate thoroughly. If it is true and established that this detestable thing has been done in Israel,
verses.tsw_comparator: and it is told to you and you hear of it, then you shall inquire carefully. And look, if the thing is true and established that this detestable thing has been done in Israel,

verses.rationale: Repeats both sexes and states the public location, method, and fatal outcome explicitly.
verses.before: then you will bring out that man or that woman who has done this evil thing to your gates—the man or the woman—and stone them with stones so that they die.
verses.after: bring the man or woman who has done this evil to your town gates. Stone that man or woman to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall bring out that man or that woman who has done this evil thing to your gates—the man or the woman—and stone them with stones so that they die.

verses.rationale: Retains the two-or-three threshold and repeats the one-witness prohibition as a distinct safeguard.
verses.before: On the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses the one who is to die will be put to death. The person will not be put to death on the mouth of one witness.
verses.after: A person may be put to death only on the testimony of two or three witnesses. No one may be put to death on the testimony of just one witness.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses the one who is to die shall be put to death. The person shall not be put to death on the mouth of one witness.

verses.rationale: Preserves witness responsibility, collective participation, and the repeated purge formula.
verses.before: The hand of the witnesses will be first against the person to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people. So you will remove the evil from your midst.
verses.after: The witnesses' hands must be the first raised to put the person to death, followed by the hands of all the people. You must purge the evil from among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hand of the witnesses shall be first against the person to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.

verses.rationale: Renders the repeated blood/blood, judgment/judgment, and lesion/lesion pairs as kinds of difficult cases; notes possible ritual scope of nega.
verses.before: “If a matter is too difficult for you in judgment, between blood and blood, between legal claim and legal claim, or between injury and injury, matters of dispute within your gates, then you will arise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
verses.after: If a case in your towns is too difficult for you to decide—whether it concerns bloodshed, legal claims, or injuries—go up to the place the LORD your God chooses.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a matter is too difficult for you in judgment, between blood and blood, between legal claim and legal claim, or between injury and injury, matters of dispute within your gates, then you shall arise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose.

verses.rationale: Keeps both the priests and contemporary judge, and the inquiry followed by their ruling.
verses.before: You will come to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in those days and inquire, and they will declare to you the word of judgment.
verses.after: Go to the Levitical priests and to the judge serving at that time. Ask them, and they will tell you the judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall come to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in those days and inquire, and they shall declare to you the word of judgment.

verses.rationale: Preserves the authoritative place and the repeated duty to carry out the instruction.
verses.before: You will act according to the word that they declare to you from that place that the LORD will choose, and you will be careful to do according to all that they instruct you.
verses.after: Act according to the decision they give you from that place the LORD chooses. Take care to do everything they instruct you to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall act according to the word that they declare to you from that place that the LORD will choose, and you shall be careful to do according to all that they instruct you.

verses.rationale: Retains torah as instruction, the judgment term, and the directional image rather than merely saying comply.
verses.before: According to the instruction that they teach you and according to the judgment that they speak to you, you will act. You will not turn aside from the word they declare to you, to the right or to the left.
verses.after: Follow the instruction they give and the judgment they pronounce. Do not turn aside from their decision, either to the right or to the left.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to the instruction that they teach you and according to the judgment that they speak to you, you shall act. You shall not turn aside from the word they declare to you, to the right or to the left.

verses.rationale: Keeps deliberate refusal, the priest's service, the alternative judge, and death as the sanction.
verses.before: The man who acts presumptuously and does not listen to the priest who stands to minister there before the LORD your God or to the judge—that man will die. So you will remove the evil from Israel.
verses.after: Anyone who acts presumptuously by refusing to listen to the priest who stands there to serve the LORD your God, or to the judge, must die. You must purge the evil from Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The man who acts presumptuously and does not listen to the priest who stands to minister there before the LORD your God or to the judge—that man shall die. So you shall remove the evil from Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves hearing and fear as the stated consequence and repeats the presumptuous-conduct term.
verses.before: All the people will hear and fear and will not act presumptuously again.
verses.after: Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and they will no longer act presumptuously.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people will hear and fear and will not act presumptuously again.

verses.rationale: Keeps entry, possession, settlement, and the people's proposed imitation of surrounding nations in their own voice.
verses.before: “When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you and possess it and live in it, and you say, ‘I will set a king over me like all the nations that are around me,’
verses.after: When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, possess it, and settle there, you may say, ‘Let us set a king over us, like all the nations around us.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you and possess it and live in it, and you say, ‘I will set a king over me like all the nations that are around me,’

verses.rationale: Preserves divine choice and the repeated kinship restriction rather than universalizing eligibility for kingship.
verses.before: you will surely set over you a king whom the LORD your God chooses. From among your brothers you will set a king over you. You may not put over you a foreign man who is not your brother.
verses.after: You must set over you a king whom the LORD your God chooses. Appoint one of your own people as king; you may not put a foreigner over you, someone who is not your fellow Israelite.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall surely set over you a king whom the LORD your God chooses. From among your brothers you shall set a king over you. You may not put over you a foreign man who is not your brother.

verses.rationale: Keeps both horse accumulation and sending people back to Egypt, followed by the quoted prohibition on return.
verses.before: Only he will not multiply horses for himself or cause the people to return to Egypt in order to multiply horses, for the LORD has said to you, ‘You will never again return by this way.’
verses.after: He must not accumulate horses for himself or send the people back to Egypt to obtain more horses. The LORD has told you, ‘You must never go back that way again.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Only he shall not multiply horses for himself or cause the people to return to Egypt in order to multiply horses, for the LORD has said to you, ‘You shall never again return by this way.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the heart-turning ground attached to many wives and the separate accumulation limit on wealth.
verses.before: He will not multiply wives for himself, lest his heart turn aside, and he will not greatly multiply silver and gold for himself.
verses.after: He must not take many wives, lest his heart turn away. Nor may he accumulate great amounts of silver and gold for himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall not multiply wives for himself, lest his heart turn aside, and he shall not greatly multiply silver and gold for himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps the king's own writing, scroll, and copy of torah; the priestly exemplar is an explicit rendering of from before the priests.
verses.before: And when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he will write for himself a copy of this instruction in a book, from before the Levitical priests.
verses.after: When he takes his royal throne, he must write for himself on a scroll a copy of this instruction, from the one kept by the Levitical priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself a copy of this instruction in a book, from before the Levitical priests.

verses.rationale: Retains possession, lifelong reading, learning fear, and practice rather than presenting the scroll as a ceremonial royal object.
verses.before: It will be with him, and he will read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, keeping all the words of this instruction and these statutes, to do them,
verses.after: It must stay with him, and he must read it all the days of his life, so that he learns to fear the LORD his God and takes care to practice all the words of this instruction and these statutes.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, keeping all the words of this instruction and these statutes, to do them,

verses.rationale: Keeps the raised-heart image of superiority, directional obedience, and the king-and-sons duration of rule.
verses.before: so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers and so that he does not turn aside from the commandment to the right or to the left, so that he may prolong days over his kingdom, he and his sons, among Israel.
verses.after: Then his heart will not rise above his fellow Israelites, and he will not turn from the command to the right or to the left. In this way he and his sons may reign long in Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers and so that he does not turn aside from the commandment to the right or to the left, in order that he may prolong days over his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the priest/tribe apposition and ishshe as offerings by fire, while distinguishing the allotted divine portion from Levi's lack of land share.
verses.before: “The Levitical priests, all the tribe of Levi, will have no portion or inheritance with Israel. They will eat the offerings by fire to the LORD and his inheritance.
verses.after: “The Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, are to have no share or inheritance with Israel. They are to eat from the LORD's offerings by fire and the portion allotted to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The Levitical priests, all the tribe of Levi, shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel. They shall eat the offerings by fire to the LORD and his inheritance.

verses.rationale: Keeps the corporate singular Levi and the repeated inheritance word, with the LORD himself as the positive counterpart.
verses.before: They will have no inheritance among their brothers. The LORD is their inheritance, as he spoke to them.
verses.after: Levi is to have no inheritance among his brothers. The LORD is his inheritance, as he promised him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall have no inheritance among their brothers. The LORD is their inheritance, as he spoke to them.

verses.rationale: Retains all three specified portions and the two-cheek number; does not substitute Leviticus' different priestly portions.
verses.before: And this will be the priest’s due from the people, from people who sacrifice an ox or sheep: they will give the priest the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach.
verses.after: This is the priests' due from the people who slaughter an ox or an animal from the flock: they must give the priest the foreleg, the two cheeks, and the stomach.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this shall be the priest’s due from the people, from those who sacrifice an ox or sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three crops and the distinct first shearing rather than reducing the list to firstfruits alone.
verses.before: The first of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the first fleece of your sheep, you will give him.
verses.after: Give him the first of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool you shear from your flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: The first of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the first fleece of your sheep, you shall give him.

verses.rationale: Preserves priestly choice from the tribes, standing service, the divine name, and enduring service through sons.
verses.before: For the LORD your God has chosen him and his sons from all your tribes to stand and minister in the name of the LORD all the days.
verses.after: For the LORD your God has chosen him and his sons from all your tribes to stand and serve in the LORD's name for all time.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God has chosen him and his sons from all your tribes to stand and minister in the name of the LORD all the days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the Levite's local residence and emphatic personal desire without turning the journey into a mandatory rotation.
verses.before: “And if a Levite comes from one of your gates, from anywhere in Israel where he sojourns, and comes with all the desire of his life to the place that the LORD will choose,
verses.after: If a Levite leaves any of your towns in Israel where he has been living and comes, with all his heart's desire, to the place the LORD chooses,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if a Levite comes from one of your gates, from anywhere in Israel where he sojourns, and comes with all the desire of his life to the place that the LORD will choose,

verses.rationale: Preserves equal participation in service alongside the Levites already standing at the sanctuary.
verses.before: then he may minister in the name of the LORD his God like all his brothers the Levites who stand there before the LORD.
verses.after: he may serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: then he may minister in the name of the LORD his God like all his brothers the Levites who stand there before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Renders the obscure ancestral-sales phrase provisionally as property proceeds, with alternatives documented rather than claiming a certain land sale.
verses.before: They will eat equal portions, besides what he receives from the sale of his ancestral property.
verses.after: He is to receive an equal share to eat, apart from the proceeds of his ancestral property.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall eat equal portions, besides what he receives from the sale of his ancestral property.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prohibition on learning the practices in the setting of entering the given land.
verses.before: “When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you will not learn to do according to the detestable practices of those nations.
verses.after: When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to practice the detestable things those nations do.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall not learn to do according to the detestable practices of those nations.

verses.rationale: Retains both children and the pass-through-fire expression, explaining its likely sacrificial force in a note; keeps four distinct practices.
verses.before: There will not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, one who practices divination, an omen-reader, a fortune-teller, a sorcerer,
verses.after: Let no one among you make a son or daughter pass through fire, practice divination, tell fortunes, read omens, or practice sorcery,
verses.tsw_comparator: There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, one who practices divination, an omen-reader, a fortune-teller, a sorcerer,

verses.rationale: Represents the remaining charm, medium, spiritist, and dead-consultation expressions without collapsing the list into magic.
verses.before: one who casts spells, one who consults a medium or a spiritist, or one who inquires of the dead.
verses.after: cast spells, consult a medium or a spiritist, or seek guidance from the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: one who casts spells, one who consults a medium or a spiritist, or one who inquires of the dead.

verses.rationale: Retains both the assessment of practitioners and the stated reason for dispossession.
verses.before: For everyone who does these things is detestable to the LORD, and because of these detestable things the LORD your God is dispossessing them before you.
verses.after: Everyone who does these things is detestable to the LORD. Because of these detestable practices, the LORD your God is driving those nations out before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For everyone who does these things is detestable to the LORD, and because of these detestable things the LORD your God is dispossessing them before you.

verses.rationale: Renders tamim as undivided integrity in this allegiance setting, with blameless as the noted alternative rather than a claim of sinless perfection.
verses.before: You will be blameless with the LORD your God.
verses.after: Be wholehearted toward the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall be blameless with the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two named practices and the contrast in what God permits; binds the full record including its source note.
verses.before: For these nations whom you are dispossessing listen to fortune-tellers and diviners, but as for you, the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
verses.after: The nations you are dispossessing listen to fortune-tellers and diviners. But the LORD your God has not permitted you to do that.
verses.tsw_comparator: For these nations whom you are dispossessing listen to fortune-tellers and diviners, but as for you, the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.

verses.rationale: Preserves singular prophet, likeness to Moses, origin within Israel, and required listening without inserting a later named fulfillment.
verses.before: “The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your midst, from your brothers. To him you will listen,
verses.after: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your fellow Israelites. You must listen to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your midst, from your brothers. To him you shall listen,

verses.rationale: Keeps Horeb, the assembly, and the source's corporate first-person singular request with its fear of death.
verses.before: according to all that you asked from the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, saying, ‘Let me not continue to hear the voice of the LORD my God or see this great fire any more, lest I die.’
verses.after: This is what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, ‘Let me not hear the voice of the LORD my God again or see this great fire anymore, or I will die.’
verses.tsw_comparator: according to all that you asked from the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, saying, ‘Let me not continue to hear the voice of the LORD my God or see this great fire any more, lest I die.’

verses.rationale: Marks the beginning of God's reply to Moses and preserves his favorable assessment of the people's request.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to me, ‘What they have spoken is good.
verses.after: The LORD said to me, ‘What they have said is good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to me, ‘What they have spoken is good.

verses.rationale: Keeps like you addressed to Moses, words placed in the prophet's mouth, and the entirety of the command.
verses.before: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will speak to them all that I command him.
verses.after: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their fellow Israelites. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him.

verses.rationale: Retains God's emphatic personal accountability and the distinction between divine words and prophetic speech.
verses.before: And it will be that whoever does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I myself will require it from him.
verses.after: I myself will hold accountable anyone who does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it will be that whoever does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I myself will require it from him.

verses.rationale: Preserves both unauthorized divine-name speech and other-god speech as separate grounds for death; closes God's quoted reply.
verses.before: But the prophet who acts presumptuously and speaks a word in my name that I did not command him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet will die.’
verses.after: But a prophet who presumes to speak in my name a word I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, must die.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But the prophet who acts presumptuously and speaks a word in my name that I did not command him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.’

verses.rationale: Returns to Moses' anticipated audience question and retains its negative formulation about a word not spoken by God.
verses.before: “And if you say in your heart, ‘How will we know the word that the LORD has not spoken?’
verses.after: You may ask yourselves, ‘How can we recognize a word the LORD has not spoken?’
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if you say in your heart, ‘How shall we know the word that the LORD has not spoken?’

verses.rationale: Keeps failed fulfillment as a negative test, with presumptuous speech and no fear; the note distinguishes this from the fulfilled-sign warning in chapter 13.
verses.before: when a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the thing does not happen or come to pass, that is a word the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. You will not fear him.
verses.after: If a prophet speaks in the LORD's name and the word does not come true or happen, the LORD has not spoken that word. The prophet has spoken presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: when a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the thing does not happen or come to pass, that is a word the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. You shall not fear him.
